paper_sections.title: Modulation of the sustained by the immediate aftereffect

description.value: The study investigated whether voluntary emotion regulation produces immediate and sustained changes in amygdala activation after active regulation has ended.

spans.text: We explored whether there would be sustained downregulation or a postregulational, paradoxical increase of amygdala activation by studying the temporal dynamics of amygdala activation in two sequenced tasks.

design.value: A within-subject fMRI study of healthy female volunteers using an active detachment-based emotion regulation task followed approximately ten minutes later by passive viewing of the same aversive and neutral visual stimuli.

spans.text: The study was composed of two tasks.
Approximately ten minutes after end of task 1, we tested for a delayed aftereffect in task 2 (“passive viewing”).

During task 1 (“active regulation”), subjects saw 60 pictures of negative or neutral content taken from the International Affective Picture System and matched for complexity and content of faces, scenery, food and nature

Subjects completed versions of the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), the State Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20) in order to rule out effects of altered mood states and deficits in emotion perception.
